title: Cover a bowl of rising dough with a cloth: draw it off a shelf with both hands so it hangs past the rim, off the dough
instruction: Cover the bowl of dough with the cloth so it can rise.
context: A small batch of bread dough (about two rolls' worth) is covered with a clean cloth while it rises so its surface does not dry into a skin. After kneading, a baker's hands are sticky, so rather than pick a cloth up and shake it open they pinch the hem of one already lying spread on a shelf behind the bowl and draw it straight over, touching only the edge. Here a terry washcloth lies on a shelf insert, 3 cm over its front edge. It is limp: it can be taken only by that short lip, with both hands about 20 cm apart, and sags once off the shelf. The robot draws it over the bowl and brings the held edge down past the near rim until the rest slides off the shelf onto the bowl, then lets go. Too little and the cloth stays stretched from the shelf; too far and it slides across the rim or drags the light glass bowl; lowered onto the bowl it presses on the dough. It must end covering the whole rim with at least 2 cm hanging past it all round, clear of the dough, with the bowl where it was.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the counter. 1) Shelf insert: IKEA VARIERA, white powder-coated steel, 320 wide (y) x 280 deep (x) x 160 high, a perforated top on four legs, open at the front; about 0.9 kg (estimate). Front edge at x = 250, centred on y = 0; its front feet on two tape marks. Top sheet 1.5 thick with 12 deep turned-down front and back edges, legs 8 x 8 (estimates). 2) Bowl: Duralex Lys 14 cm, clear tempered glass, 140 across the rim, 55 high, 500 ml; foot 70 across, wall 4.5, bottom 6 (estimates that give the 500 ml); about 270 g (estimate). Foot centred at (150, 0), so its far rim is 30 from the shelf. 3) Dough stand-in: one 4 oz (112 g) can of white Play-Doh pressed into the bottom as a centred dome 80 across and 26 high, its top 23 below the rim (shape it by ruler). 4) Cloth: one Burt's Bees Baby organic cotton woven terry washcloth, Blue Solid, 254 x 254 (10 x 10 in), about 29 g and 2.5 thick (estimates). It lies flat and square on the shelf, smooth face up, hems parallel to x and y, centred on y = 0, its near edge 30 past the shelf's front edge (x = 220 before it droops); the lip's tip droops about 8 below the shelf top (estimate). Start: both arms at their ready pose, grippers open. Frictions are estimates (cloth 1.5 in the simulator, shelf 0.35, glass 0.45).
scoring: Judged at the end of the run from the top-camera video, a top photo, a side photo through the clear bowl with a ruler stood behind it, and a flexible tape. A part of the rim is covered when, in the top photo, the cloth hides it. Overhang: along the cloth from the rim's outer edge to the nearest cloth edge, where it is shortest. Score 0 if either gripper still holds the cloth or is within 2 cm of it, the cloth is still moving (any point more than 5 mm in the last 5 s; in simulation any node more than 1 cm in the last second), no part of the rim is covered (doing nothing scores 0), the bowl tipped more than 15 degrees at any time, or the bowl's centre moved more than 2 cm. Otherwise the lowest of: (1) rim covered: 1.0 if all of it; 0.5 if at least 75 % but not all; 0.25 if under 75 %. (2) shortest overhang: 1.0 if at least 2 cm; 0.75 if at least 1 cm and under 2 cm; 0.5 if under 1 cm. (3) bowl moved: 1.0 if at most 1 cm; 0.75 if more than 1 cm. (4) dough: 1.0 if the cloth does not touch the dough and its lowest point inside the rim is at most 1.5 cm below the rim's top; 0.75 if it does not touch but hangs lower; 0.5 if it touches. (5) shelf: 1.0 if no part of the cloth lies on the shelf insert's top; 0.25 if some does. Simulation checks the rim every 5 degrees; touching = a cloth node within 2.75 mm of the dome.
reset_notes: About 2 minutes. Lift the cloth off by hand. Stand the bowl back with its foot centred at (150, 0) on its pencil circle; if the cloth touched the dough, re-shape the Play-Doh dome by ruler (80 across, 26 high, top 23 below the rim). Keep the Play-Doh in its can between sessions and use a fresh can after 10 trials or when it cracks or dries. Shake the cloth out and lay it flat and square on the shelf top, smooth face up, centred, with 30 mm of its near edge past the shelf's front edge (ruler), no folds. Use a fresh cloth from the pack when it is creased, damp or marked, and after 20 trials; wash and dry used ones before reuse. Check the shelf insert's front feet are on their tape marks. Both arms to the ready pose, grippers open.
fidelity: The cloth is true PhysX cloth (1,369 nodes); its bend stiffness makes the 30 mm lip droop about 8 mm at rest, as estimated for the real cloth. While both pads press the cloth it is pinned to the gripper (PhysX cloth has no static friction); opening releases it, and nothing else does. Once let go, its hem may tremble a few mm for seconds, so stillness is judged over 1 s. The dough is a rigid dome in the bowl; the shelf is fixed. Masses, thicknesses, droop and frictions are estimates.
